markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Repeated textual agreement may distinguish specific interests from broad resemblance. Distinct IDs alone do not prevent product variants or boilerplate from manufacturing support. (2) A semantic residual supplies an inspectable connection to history. Similarity cannot establish compatibility, added capability, or present demand. (3) Multi-negative training challenges ranking errors. Electronics’ 16.98% sampled-pair error motivates testing it, without predicting validation gains.

**Related-work insights.** (1) gSASRec [1] motivates objective calibration; sampling comparisons [2] caution against assuming harder negatives help. These justify a loss-only control. (2) FSASA [3] separates recent and global preferences. Recency-sensitive TF–IDF [6] and established content profiles [5] make the proposed components familiar, limiting novelty claims. (3) MERLIN [4] distinguishes directional associations from resemblance. Its unavailable relationship supervision prevents interpreting lexical agreement as compatibility evidence. (4) UniT [7] motivates caution about semantic concentration. Product-variant redundancy [8] motivates shortcut controls, although neither establishes failure here.

### Framework

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Unresolved limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking objective | gBCE; sampling comparisons [1,2] | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Training errors need not track HR@10 |
| Current, specific intent | Local/global fusion; content profiles [3,5,6] | Recent, repeated lexical support | Emerging interests lack repetition |
| Useful successors | Asymmetric associations [4] | Shrunk directed-transition residual | Transitions do not prove compatibility |
| Evidence quality | Semantic concentration; variant redundancy [7,8] | Boilerplate and duplicate-support controls | Lexical specificity can still mislead |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are hypotheses, not results. O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell gives score and positive/negative rationale.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Uniform multi-negative softmax [1,2] | 2; clear control / established | 7; reusable / limited mechanism | 3; sharper ranking / no intent signal | 8; challenges errors / surrogate only | 2; localized / masking required |
| B: Recency-and-repeat lexical residual [3,5,6] | 4; calibrated combination / established components | 7; interpretable foundation / lexical limits | 8; specificity and freshness / compatibility unresolved | 7; combined-score training / transfer uncertain | 5; fixed features / causal sparse integration |
| C: Directed-transition residual [4] | 4; directional evidence / established approach | 7; successor modeling / sparse edges | 7; task continuity / accidental transitions | 6; discriminative signal / popularity confounding | 5; sparse counts / prefix leakage risk |

### Selected idea: B

At 10% progress, retain fixed TF–IDF rather than adding a learned encoder. Recency addresses outdated interests; repeated specific evidence addresses broad associations and unexplained recommendations. Combined-score softmax targets sampled ranking errors, especially Electronics. These are mechanisms to test, not demonstrated user benefits.

```text
Fit training-only TF–IDF; cache normalized sparse item rows.
For each causal prefix: deduplicate recent IDs; compute recency × cross-item agreement.
Normalize their weighted text pool; compute support confidence separately.
score = SASRec + projected_alpha × confidence × pool_dot_candidate.
Train combined-score uniform multi-negative softmax; project alpha into [0,A].
```

Return zero for unsupported pools. Initialize alpha directly at zero: squared mappings stall there; confidence must follow normalization. Never form catalog-wide X Xᵀ. First compare fixed-checkpoint last-item, uniform, recency, support, and shrinkage variants; then baseline, loss-only, and combined training. Mask inferred brands, remove recurring templates, and merge near-duplicate support votes in diagnostic ablations without changing splits.

Predeclare trials, checkpoints, stopping rules, and a practical improvement threshold within 43,200 cumulative GPU-seconds. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnosis compatibility, and predictor parity. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10; report paired dataset differences and exploratory stratified bootstrap intervals. Training margins, sampled HR, and searched-winner intervals cannot establish full-catalog gains or eliminate adaptive-selection bias [9,10].

idea.description: Add a bounded lexical residual to per-dataset SASRec using recency-weighted agreement across distinct recent historical items, with support confidence applied after pool normalization. Start with fixed training-only TF–IDF and train the combined scorer with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale interests, broad associations, and recommendations without an identifiable historical connection. Recency weighting and repeated lexical support directly target these separate failures. Combined-score training addresses the observed positive–negative ranking errors, particularly Electronics’ 16.98% error rate, without treating training diagnostics as evidence of validation improvement. Compatibility, complementary usefulness, and satisfied demand remain unresolved because lexical resemblance does not establish them.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain all four datasets and dataset routing; DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], with artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, unchanged splits and pinned candidates, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with default 200. Use one GPU per trial and charge concurrent trials cumulatively against 43,200 GPU-seconds.

Fit separate per-dataset TF–IDF vocabularies and IDF statistics using permitted titles/descriptions of training-observed items only. A reproducible initial configuration is lowercase word unigrams/bigrams, sublinear term frequency, minimum document frequency 2, maximum document frequency 0.95, maximum 50,000 features, and L2 normalization; persist the complete vectorizer configuration. Transform other catalog metadata using the frozen vocabulary, allowing zero rows for missing or entirely out-of-vocabulary text. Store float32 CSR rows. Metadata has no guaranteed historical snapshot, so do not claim timestamp-level text availability.

For every valid training position, use only its causal input prefix, including the current input item but excluding the future target event. Do not delete earlier occurrences merely because their ID equals the target: that would make features label-dependent and inconsistent with inference. Within the last K events, retain each distinct item's latest occurrence and its actual event age. Begin with K=20, event half-life h=5, and shrinkage lambda=1 as declared starting settings, not validated optima. For m distinct items, agreement a_j is mean nonnegative TF–IDF cosine against the other m−1 items; set all agreement to zero when m<2. Define r_j=2^(-age_j/h), w_j=r_j*a_j, S=sum(w_j), normalized pool p=normalize(sum(w_j*x_j)), and confidence c=S/(S+lambda). Return p=0 and c=0 when support or pool norm is zero. Apply c after normalization: normalizing c*p would cancel confidence. Deduplicating IDs does not remove near-duplicate products; include a fixed, training-derived text-fingerprint grouping as a diagnostic support-vote control. Keep its grouping rule and threshold explicit and frozen.

Use score=f_ID+alpha*c*dot(p,x_i). Optimize alpha directly, initialized exactly at zero, then project it into [0,A] under no_grad after every optimizer step; exclude it from weight decay. Its score derivative is c*dot(p,x_i), permitting useful loss gradients at zero. Squared or tanh-squared parameterizations stall at zero; sigmoid and softplus cannot provide exact zero with a useful finite-parameter derivative. A starting cap A=1 is a scale-sensitive hypothesis, so log ID-logit scale and include zero in the preregistered cap comparison. Fixed text pooling needs no gradients. If learned pooling is later introduced, sparse backward support and the initial zero gradients to content-only parameters require a separate implementation.

Begin with M=32 independent eligible uniform negatives per valid position, sampled with replacement; record M and duplicate handling. Exclude padding, the target, and observed training positives using training data only. Skip positions with no eligible negatives. This filtered sampled-softmax objective is a ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-catalog likelihood; do not add an unverified logQ correction. Keep SASRec architecture, optimizer, and checkpoint schedule matched for baseline and loss-only controls; record all effective settings inherited from the template.

Compute agreement only within bounded recent windows, never as catalog-wide X Xᵀ. Construct sparse history-weight matrices H and multiply H*X, normalizing rows before applying confidence. Score sampled items through sparse intersections or bounded dense buffers. For full-catalog unseen-item recommendations, score catalog blocks, mask observed history items, and retain running top-k with deterministic tie handling. Provide this path for the twenty simulator users without interpreting simulator diversity/conformity traits as observed.

Use fixed SASRec checkpoints and identical candidates to compare last-item TF–IDF, uniform recent pooling, recency pooling, distinct-item agreement, and confidence shrinkage before expensive combined training. Compare unchanged SASRec, loss-only, and the residual with a small preregistered trial list. Run title-inferred brand masking, recurring-description removal, and near-duplicate support-vote controls as diagnostic ablations; these are imperfect lexical controls, not verified brand or product-family labels. Count terms once per distinct item when estimating support. Preserve unsupported histories as a reported slice rather than silently excluding them.

Predeclare checkpoint queries, stopping rules, a practical improvement threshold, and the selection/tie rule before observing new validation results. An illustrative budget is 8,640 GPU-seconds baseline/calibration, 21,600 ablations, 8,640 finalist confirmation, and 4,320 diagnostics/failures. These are cumulative allocations, not additional budgets; stop admitting trials that cannot fit the remaining allowance. Record every trial and validation query. Fixed-seed reruns assess reproducibility, not seed robustness.

Use the pinned evaluator's four-category macro validation HR@10 for selection. Where its existing outputs expose paired per-user hits, report dataset HR, paired differences, discordant wins/losses, and 10,000 within-dataset paired bootstrap draws using a recorded analysis seed. Do not modify the host evaluator to obtain them; report unavailable uncertainty analyses as unavailable. One changed user hit changes dataset HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Intervals are exploratory and conditional on trained models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed variability, candidate variability, and adaptive-selection bias. Freeze the selected configuration before independent held-out evaluation. No test labels or test metrics enter search.

Persist vocabulary, IDF, item features, pooling and confidence settings, alpha, architecture configuration, weights, mappings, and routing; update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reproduces trained scores. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must remain the actual trained nn.Module; retain item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility. Carry causal text states with SASRec states through the adapter so diagnostic positive/negative scores include the deployed residual, while preserving expected sequence shapes. Restore model mode after probes and use eval/no_grad. Report item-embedding alignment as a descriptive statistic, not proof of collapse. No reviews, ratings, categories, prices, stores, pretrained weights, extra datasets, or hidden test files are required.
idea.pseudocode:
For each routed dataset:
    fit and freeze training-only TFIDF; cache normalized float32 CSR catalog rows X
    initialize SASRec as baseline; alpha = directly optimized scalar 0
    for each training batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
        h = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
        for each nonpadding prediction position t:
            prefix = sequence through t; never inspect positive[t] to construct prefix features
            ids, ages = latest-occurrence deduplication within prefix[-K:]
            z = X[ids]
            a[j] = mean(dot(z[j], z[k]) for k != j), or 0 if fewer than two ids
            w[j] = 2**(-ages[j]/half_life) * a[j]
            S = sum(w)
            p = normalize(sum(w[j]*z[j])), or zero
            c = S/(S+lambda), or zero if pool is empty
            candidates = positive[t] plus M eligible uniform training-only negatives
            logits = ID_scores(h[t], candidates) + alpha*c*dot(p, X[candidates])
        optimize mean cross_entropy(logits, positive_index=0)
        under no_grad: alpha.clamp_(0, A)
    evaluate only at preregistered checkpoints with the pinned evaluator
Compare fixed-checkpoint pooling ablations, unchanged SASRec, loss-only, and combined training.
Select using four-category macro validation HR@10 and the declared tie rule.
Export all artifacts and the matching predictor writer; verify train/inference score parity.
For simulator users: blockwise full-catalog scoring, observed-item masking, running top-k.

originality.positive: The particular combination of causal distinct-item agreement, explicit recency, confidence shrinkage, and a projected lexical residual is a plausible incremental contribution under this restricted benchmark.
originality.negative: TF–IDF user profiles, temporal weighting, local/global preferences, and additive scoring are established. The supplied search does not demonstrate that this exact combination is unprecedented.

future_potential.positive: A small, inspectable mechanism supports controlled research on when recurring textual evidence improves current-interest ranking, with clear extensions to directional evidence.
future_potential.negative: Boilerplate and product variants can create shortcuts; repetition can suppress new interests, and lexical evidence cannot verify compatibility, satisfied needs, or complementary capability.

code_difficulty.positive: Fixed text features avoid another learned encoder and auxiliary objective, while a single residual coefficient limits model complexity.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal sparse pooling, exact confidence placement, negative eligibility, blockwise catalog scoring, diagnostic compatibility, and predictor parity require substantial care beyond a localized loss change.

related_work.title: gSASRec (2024 extended abstract) [1]
contributions: Attributes part of SASRec overconfidence to sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE.
Motivates an objective-only control before adding architecture.
limitations: Does not establish gains under this pinned four-category evaluation.
Objective calibration alone does not explicitly address stale interests or broad lexical associations.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): negative-sampling comparisons [2]
contributions: Compares uniform, popularity, in-batch, mixed, and adaptive negative sampling.
Motivates uniform multi-negative training as an essential control.
limitations: Sampling effectiveness and popularity effects depend on the dataset.
Harder negatives cannot be assumed to improve the host's fixed-candidate HR@10.

related_work.title: FSASA (2024) [3]
contributions: Combines global SASRec preference with a session-aware local branch and GRU-based weighting.
Motivates distinguishing recent intent from older preference.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed repeated-support lexical residual.
The supplied evidence establishes no improvement on this exact benchmark.

related_work.title: MERLIN (CIKM 2024) [4]
contributions: Models asymmetric item associations using separate source and destination representations.
Motivates distinguishing resemblance from directional purchase usefulness.
limitations: Its association supervision cannot be assumed available from this task's interaction histories.
Lexical agreement does not recover verified complementarity or compatibility labels.

related_work.title: Pazzani and Billsus (2007): Content-Based Recommendation Systems [5]
contributions: Describes established content profiles and TF–IDF representations for recommendation.
Provides a direct precedent for pooling item text into user preference representations.
limitations: Does not establish novelty or effectiveness of the proposed causal support calibration.
Does not validate this SASRec residual under the pinned evaluation.

related_work.title: Marwah and Beel (2020): time-normalized TF–IDF [6]
contributions: Compares time-normalized TF–IDF with ordinary TF–IDF across three retrieval datasets.
Supports investigating recency-sensitive lexical weighting.
limitations: Retrieval results do not establish sequential-recommendation gains.
Time-normalized term weighting differs from the proposed history-event recency weighting.

related_work.title: UniT (2025) [7]
contributions: Documents excessive clustering of semantically similar item representations.
Motivates testing whether repeated similarity reinforces narrow or redundant evidence.
limitations: Does not establish that this task's embedding statistics indicate collapse.
Does not directly test fixed TF–IDF residuals or boilerplate controls here.

related_work.title: Basaran et al. (2017): Amazon product-variant redundancy [8]
contributions: Shows that product-variant redundancies can distort evaluation and algorithm rankings.
Motivates distinguishing distinct IDs from independent supporting evidence.
limitations: Its rating-prediction setting does not quantify redundancy exposure in this benchmark.
Text-based near-duplicate groups are imperfect proxies for product variants.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation [9]
contributions: Explains limitations of sampled recommendation metrics, including possible reversals of model comparisons.
Supports separating pinned sampled-candidate selection from full-catalog claims.
limitations: Does not invalidate the mandated host metric as the task's selection criterion.
Does not supply full-catalog evidence for the proposed model.

related_work.title: Cawley and Talbot (2010): overfitting in model selection [10]
contributions: Explains model-selection overfitting and resulting evaluation bias.
Motivates limited preregistered comparisons, complete trial logs, and frozen selection before held-out evaluation.
limitations: Ordinary bootstrap intervals do not remove adaptive-selection bias.
A fixed training seed does not measure robustness across training randomness.

related_work.title: PyTorch sparse.mm documentation
contributions: Documents sparse matrix multiplication capabilities and backward restrictions.
Supports fixed sparse pooling and highlights the need to verify layout-specific gradient support before learning history weights.
limitations: Sparse-by-sparse backward is unsupported.
Sparse output can still become large; documentation does not guarantee efficiency for this workload.

related_work.title: scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: Defines vocabulary fitting, IDF weighting, tokenization settings, and row normalization.
L2-normalized rows make dot products cosine similarities.
limitations: Normalization removes multiplicative confidence applied before normalization.
TF–IDF cannot independently establish compatibility or semantic understanding.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling for related observations.
Supports resampling paired user hits independently within each dataset before computing macro differences.
limitations: Intervals require assumptions about user exchangeability.
They exclude adaptive search bias, training variability, and fixed-candidate sampling variability; sparse discordances can yield unstable intervals.

related_work.title: PyTorch Softplus documentation
contributions: Defines a positive smooth transformation.
Helps explain why direct projected optimization is preferable when exact zero residual initialization is required.
limitations: Softplus does not attain exact zero at finite inputs mathematically.
Very negative initialization can make the gradient extremely small.

related_work.title: TASTE (2023)
contributions: Compares text-only and identifier-plus-text modeling and reports reduced popularity bias.
Provides qualitative motivation for examining broad brand associations versus product-type relevance.
limitations: Uses pretrained T5, which is outside this task's permitted proposal.
Its qualitative brand example is not a controlled brand-removal ablation or evidence for this benchmark.

related_work.title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains risks from repeatedly adapting hypotheses to holdout feedback.
Motivates restrained validation access and explicit separation of search from final evaluation.
limitations: The proposed experiment does not implement a reusable-holdout mechanism.
Logging and limiting queries reduce exposure but do not themselves guarantee unbiased selected-model estimates.
